text_to_speech: the king can move one square in any direction the King cannot move to a square where an opposing piece can capture it the Queen can move back and forth sideways and diagonally in any direction the rook can move back and forth in sideways but not diagonally each Bishop can only move diagonally and only on one color the knight moves in an L pattern one space then two or two spaces then one in any direction the knight is the only piece that can move through another piece a pond moves only forward one space except on the first move when it can go one or two spaces ponds capture diagonally if a pond moves two spaces to avoid capture by another pond the other pond can take the first one as if it only moved one space this is called on peasant French for in passing if neither the King nor rook have moved then there are no pieces between them they can castle the king can castle to either side where their pawns are present or not enjoy playing chess

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The king can move one square in any direction. The king cannot move to a square where an opposing
piece can capture it. The queen can move back and forth sideways and diagonally in any direction.
The rook can move back and forth in sideways but not diagonally. Each bishop can only move diagonally
and only on one color. The knight moves in an L pattern, one space then two or two spaces then one in any direction.
The knight is the only piece that can move through another piece. A pawn moves only forward one space except on the first move when it can go one or two spaces.

Pond's capture diagonally. If a pawn moves two spaces to avoid capture by another pawn the other pawn can take the first one as if it only moved one space. This is called on pass-on, French, for in passing.
If neither the king nor rook have moved then there are no pieces between them they can castle. The king can castle to either side where their pawns are present or not.
